gen-dafont-franchise-gf-judson: Dignified and bookish, Judson fills the body with stencil-bold stems and fine scribed hairlines. Franchise is strong and clean on top, a single-nib look that crowds its letters tight, and Judson is where the thick-thin drama turns all the way up.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-naskh-arabi: Franchise stands tall and tightly packed, its strokes like thread stitched along a path. And Noto Naskh Arabic follows with a refined classic serif, lightly engraved in feel, with a very tall x-height and no harsh thin spots.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-nastaliq-ur: Noto Nastaliq Urdu reads tight and editorial, its serif strokes differing just enough to feel alive. Noto Nastaliq Urdu against Franchise, which has no hairlines anywhere, makes the pair's strongest quality a clear split between uniform line and living stroke.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-rashi-hebre: Bookish and classic, Noto Rashi Hebrew moves like a lightly tilted nib, soft and steady, on tall lowercase bodies. But Franchise does its best work as a constant-width outline you could trace with a finger, while the classic serif body handles the quiet, engraved detail.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-ahom: Tall, tubular and tightly packed. Franchise gives every stroke a pipe-like body, while Noto Serif Ahom adds gentle swelling on its curves, and its lofty text serif lowercase can be sized up a notch for comfort.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-armen: Noto Serif Armenian reads open and approachable, with big counters and mild contrast. Its strongest quality is the way that worn felt-marker swelling sits beside Franchise, whose neon-tube strokes never change width at all.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-balin: Franchise looks like glass tubing bent into tall, tightly crowded letters, strong and clean. Noto Serif Balinese follows with strokes that taper only slightly, like a candle flame, and that gives the pair its strongest quality: a steady mid-contrast under a rigid heading.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-benga: Tall, tight and strong, Franchise traces each letter in a line of constant weight, so every stroke feels drawn with one pen. It earns its keep big and short, with Noto Serif Bengali's refined hairlines left for elsewhere.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-devan: Classic and literary, Noto Serif Devanagari slims its horizontals just below its verticals, with short ascenders and a big lowercase body. But Franchise holds one pen width throughout, so a long stretch of text would feel like a quiet, bookish voice under a firm one.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-dives: Noto Serif Dives Akuru is classic and refined. Franchise builds its uppercase from lines of one constant thickness, strong and clean, while the serif body softens every curve with hairline-free thin strokes beside moderately weighty stems.
